extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, European patent attorneys, IP practitioners advising on EPO filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal requirements for filing colour or greyscale drawings with the European Patent Office (including interactions with PCT/Euro‑PCT, added‑matter, divisionals and missing parts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings execution requirement (Article 1(2)(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Original rule text: "Drawings shall be executed without colourings in durable, black, sufficiently dense and dark, uniformly thick and well-defined lines and strokes. When filed by means of electronic communication, drawings may also be executed in colour or in greyscale, in durable, uniformly thick and well-defined lines, strokes or areas [...]"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colour/greyscale are now permitted for electronically filed drawings but drawings must still be durable and use uniformly thick and well-defined lines/strokes/areas. This is a primary formal/legal baseline for admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast and resolution requirement (300 dpi)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice requires that colour or greyscale drawings "must also be sufficiently rich in contrast and suitable to be clearly displayed at a resolution of 300 dpi."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory formal requirement subject to examination by the EPO Receiving Section (citing Rule 57(i) EPC). Ensure submitted images have adequate contrast and are legible at 300 dpi to avoid refusal or formal objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Section formal examination (Rule 57(i) EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO's Receiving Section will formally examine whether drawings comply with the contrast/300 dpi requirement, citing Rule 57(i) EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect a formal check at filing and prepare drawings that demonstrably meet the stated standards to avoid processing delays or requests for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings‑only limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of colour or greyscale is strictly limited to the drawings. The Notice is unambiguous that the use of colour or greyscale in the description, claims, or abstract is inadmissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the description, claims or abstract are filed with colour, those elements will be converted to black and white for publication. Applicants must therefore confine colour to the drawings themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory: avoid referring to colours in text ("Don't Say Red")
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are advised not to refer to colour‑specific features of the drawings in the description, claims or abstract (e.g. stating a component is "beige" or "yellow"), since colour specifications may not always be reliably and objectively identifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make claim or description language depend on colour-based distinctions. Instead, describe features by structure, material, position, or other non-colour attributes to avoid clarity/sufficiency problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT international phase inadmissibility of colour drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Colour drawings are not admissible under the PCT in the international phase; any colour drawings filed in a PCT application are rendered in black and white by the International Bureau (IB) for international publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants filing PCT applications should be aware that the international publication will be in B&W even if colour originals are filed; plan drafting and cross-referencing accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: PATENTSCOPE retention and publication flagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the IB renders drawings in B&W for international publication, it will retain the original colour/greyscale version and make it available on PATENTSCOPE; the cover page of the international publication will indicate this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The original colour drawings may be accessible via PATENTSCOPE, but availability must be explicitly flagged in the international publication for downstream offices (like the EPO) to rely on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO reliance on colour drawings for Euro‑PCT: two conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: For Euro‑PCT applications entering the European phase on or after 1 October 2025, the EPO will base its processing on the colour drawings only if (1) they are available on PATENTSCOPE AND (2) the international publication mentions this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If either condition is not met, the EPO's processing "will be based on the drawings as published in black and white." Applicants must ensure both availability on PATENTSCOPE and proper indication in the international publication to have the EPO treat the colour drawings as the basis for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 123(2) EPC (added matter) check for post‑publication colour filings
rubrics_metrics.description: For Euro‑PCT applications that entered the phase before 1 October 2025 (and are thus B&W), if the applicant subsequently files colour drawings, the EPO "will examine compliance with Article 123(2) EPC."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing colour drawings after an earlier B&W publication may raise added‑matter issues. Ensure that newly filed colour illustrations do not introduce subject‑matter that extends beyond the content of the earlier filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 76(1) EPC (divisionals) scrutiny for colour drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: For divisional applications filed with colour drawings, the EPO will "carefully check" compliance with Article 76(1) EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing a divisional that includes colour drawings, verify that the drawings and any claimed subject‑matter comply with the divisional requirements to avoid objections based on added matter or basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing parts (Rule 56): drawings must match priority content/format
rubrics_metrics.description: If filing missing parts, the drawings must "correspond exactly to the content and format" of the priority application. If the priority had B&W drawings, the missing drawings must also be B&W.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When remedying missing parts, ensure the drawings submitted exactly replicate the content and format of the priority documents (including colour vs B&W) to preserve priority and avoid formal objections.
